newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Corrupt Brazil policemen sell guns to bandits - TV.
newsitem.headline: Corrupt Brazil policemen sell guns to bandits - TV.

text.p: Corrupt Brazilian policemen have set up a sophisticated network selling government arms and ammunition to clients including drug traffickers and bandits, Globo television said on Monday.

"We don't go to Miami, we don't go looking in New York, the people who bring us these arms are policemen themselves," a man wearing a ski-mask and wielding a machine-gun told Globo in a Rio de Janeiro shantytown.
Corruption is rife among Brazilian police, and many say low salaries are to blame.
Globo showed hidden camera footage in which a man, identified as a federal policeman, concluded an arms deal in broad daylight on a Rio de Janeiro beach.
The man was shown putting a Ruger machine-gun wrapped in a black trash bag onto the back seat of the buyer's car and taking a cash payment of $3,500.

Globo also set up an arms deal at a Rio de Janeiro hotel, at which an ex-policeman sold a 45-mm. weapon, AK and AR rifles and ammunition to a man purporting to be a farmer. Brazilian landowners frequently hire private security guards to protect their land from invasions by landless peasants.
